newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Treasury will seek further budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Israel Treasury will seek further budget cuts.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that the government would propose to parliament an additional two billion shekels in 1997 budget cuts by early December.

"We're at a very difficult crossroads," he told reporters after meeting with Finance Minister Dan Meridor. "We received a difficult legacy from the previous government, but how difficult became apparent only in recent days."

The additional spending reductions will come on top of 4.9 billion shekels the government has already submitted to parliament. The supplementary cuts will now be incorporated into the original budget package.

The government has been hinting for some time that further cuts would have to be made to keep the budget deficit from breaching the Treasury's target. On Tuesday Meridor confirmed the Treasury would seek cuts of about two billion shekels.

Netanyahu and Meridor did not say where the additional cuts would come from, but vowed they would not raise taxes as an alternative. "We will do everything not to increase the tax burden. We already have one of the highest tax burdens in the world," said Netanyahu.
Final plans will be worked out after November 30, when the latest revenue figures are in and a proposal will be given to parliament in early December.

The government already faces tough opposition in parliament to the original cuts. But this year's budget is running well in excess of the deficit target as government revenues have fallen behind projections.
